news.title: James Gosling, creator of Java, asked by Navin Reddy whether he codes with AI (somewhat cl…
news.author: firstprimate@kolektiva.social
news.snippet: James Gosling, creator of Java, asked by Navin Reddy whether he codes with AI (somewhat cleaned up from the transcript): "NR And do you use AI to do that? JG: I have played with AI tools and I mostly find them to be really annoying. I mean, the thing is that I know how to write software. Um, and every time I've used an AI tool, I I look at the software that it generates and for the most part it's just awful. And I care about how evolvable a piece of software is, how reliable it is, you know, how testable it is. And I have yet to find a coding system that works for me cuz it just all you know it all feels like a really great demo, just not ready for prime time. NR: So do you think there will be a day when AI can reach there? JG: Oh maybe, kind of, but why? I mean you know in the spectrum of problems in the so in software engineering, coding has never really been a big problem. The places where there are problems are in like testing. How do you know that this piece of software actually does what you need it to do? That's a really really difficult problem. That's a problem that is unpleasant. It burns a lot of a lot of time. And you you know, everything I've seen about AI tools just is that they just make hard problem worse. And the the easy problem, yeah, marginally better. But also the easy problem is also the enjoyable problem. So I view AI in part as stealing the fun and making the torture worse. And you know, people go, "Well, you know, I wrote up this little Swift iPhone app. Doesn't that count?" And it's like, "I don't care, right? I mean, small toy apps like that are are nothing. I mean, I'm, you know, software doesn't get interesting until it's got like until it's like millions of lines, right? You know, until you're doing something like, you know, operating FedEx, right? Right. You know, and you know, some, you know, a place like FedEx, you know, they've got hundreds of thousands of llines of code, probably actually probably millions of lines of code and, you know, 100 000 engineers. I mean, it's a really complicated thing to run a business like Uber or FedEx or UPS or a bank. And building software suites like that is is where there's difficulty, you know, glossing up, you know, a Swift app to take a survey. Okay, that's fine. But that's not a problem. NR: That's right. So when you're building a give it business where you have as you mentioned million lines of code and then we have entire team I mean teams of team who is working together to get the one thing that's where it excels JG: where what excels? NR: the human JG: oh yeah I mean when when it when things get complicated you need people. I have not seen a scrap of evidence that the AI coding tools, you know, if if you wanted to build the next FedEx and you were just going to vibe code the next FedEx, I think you'd be in trouble. NR: Yeah. Yeah. You never know when you have security flaw and getting hacked. JG: Yeah. Yeah. O when when your AI tools decide, you know, the best way to be profitable is to steal money from all your customers. Because you know then people have tried to to to do experiments like have AI just run a single vending machine as a business or do security penetration experiments inside inside a company and then you discover that all hell breaks loose, right? Um these these things are a very, very long way from being deployable at scale with a decent amount of faith that things will work out." https:// youtu.be/LxhZhOOYKTM?t=513 # AI # Java # SoftwareDevelopment # SoftwareEngineering
